sources.title: Warp Agent CLI
sources.finding: Standalone warp command runs the native agent in any terminal including SSH, with saved account conversations, shell, diffs, approvals, context and model selection.

sources.title: Warp Agent CLI quickstart
sources.finding: CLI supports macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Linux x64/Arm64 and Windows x64/Arm64. Browser device code or WARP_API_KEY authentication is documented.

sources.title: Third-party CLI agents overview
sources.finding: Warp detects third-party coding agents in terminal panes with rich input, per-agent status, code review and remote control. They are separate from the native conversation and agent-management panels.

sources.title: Set up Claude Code
sources.finding: Warp documents running Claude Code with a paid Claude account or API credits and authenticating with its own provider login.

sources.title: Agent Session Sharing
sources.finding: Local Warp and third-party sessions can be shared to signed-in web/mobile viewers. Editors can prompt and execute commands concurrently; data expires after roughly one week and secret redaction is not applied.

sources.title: Agent planning and execution
sources.finding: Plans are editable, versioned, selectively executable and saved in Warp Drive with Markdown export and reuse across conversations.

sources.title: Agent Task Lists
sources.finding: The agent creates sequential task lists automatically for complex requests and shows pending, active, completed and cancelled statuses inside conversations.

sources.title: Rules for agents
sources.finding: Global and repository AGENTS.md/WARP.md rules have documented precedence and create/edit/delete controls. WARP.md wins when both exist in one directory.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol
sources.finding: Warp local agents support command, Streamable HTTP and SSE MCP servers, credentials via env/headers, and local configuration; launched servers stop when Warp exits.

sources.title: Codebase Context
sources.finding: Git-tracked repositories and worktrees index separately; code is not stored on Warp servers. Sync is periodic, at new conversations or manual; indexing delay can expose stale context.

sources.title: Git worktrees
sources.finding: Warp supports separate Git worktrees with independent diffs, indexing and branch status for parallel local agent work.

sources.title: Running orchestrated agents
sources.finding: A Warp app parent proposes a child-agent breakdown through /orchestrate or /plan. Approved children can run locally or in cloud environments, with status pills and retained child conversations.

sources.title: Profiles & Permissions
sources.finding: Profiles configure models and per-tool autonomy, command allow/denylists and MCP tool access. Run-until-completion can bypass denylist prompts for a task.

sources.title: Roles and permissions
sources.finding: Owner, Admin and Member have explicit administration and usage boundaries; organization-enforced settings cannot be overridden.

sources.title: Privacy and data control
sources.finding: Paid plans may disable Help improve Warp and crash reports while retaining AI. Free AI requires telemetry. Vendor documentation labels client source AGPLv3, but its linked source license was not retrievable in this pass.

sources.title: Architecture and deployment
sources.finding: Warp separates client/execution from its hosted orchestration, observability and inference control plane; customer-hosted workers still send prompts/transcripts through Warp servers.

sources.title: Warp Trust Center
sources.finding: Vendor states SOC2 TypeII covering security, availability, confidentiality and processing integrity; Enterprise reports are request-only. No audit issuer/period was exposed.

sources.title: Interactive Code Review
sources.finding: Inline comments on Git-indexed diffs can be batched and sent to native or supported third-party agents for revisions.

sources.title: Agent conversations in Warp Agent CLI
sources.finding: Conversations save automatically, sync across account clients and resume after exiting. Markdown export and Ctrl+C cancellation are documented; restoring a process is separate.
